solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mixed rum cup: it's so delightful!

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the words that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a rum punch and declares it wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' is the anagram signal working on RUMCUPITSSO; the exclamation in the surface is just enthusiasm for the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal praise, synonyms for something highly pleasing, especially food or drink.

clue.text: Resentful about conductor's original musical arrangement

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second, wrapping it

parts.note: feeling sore is feeling aggrieved or resentful

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter, here of conductor's

explanation.surface: A bitter musician complains about how the conductor first arranged a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C, the first letter of 'conductor's' given by 'original', inside SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written version of a composition, setting out the parts for each instrument.

clue.text: Listens during actual practice session

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time span, so inside, of the other

parts.note: something actual is real
to hear is to listen, so listens gives hears

explanation.surface: A coach pays attention while a real training session goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is a time word used here for position: one word sits within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a trial run of a performance, the practice before the real show.

clue.text: Trading place, home for a bird

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place for trading
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: A market stall serves as somewhere a bird can nest.
explanation.walkthrough: IN for 'home' is a crossword staple: someone at home is in.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin and sand martin are small swallow-like birds, so this is an example.

clue.text: Almost level in cup match

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tier is a level or layer, as in a tiered cake

explanation.surface: A football fixture finishes nearly all square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from TIER. In Britain a cup tie is a knockout match in a competition like the FA Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie in British sport is a single fixture in a knockout competition, like a round of the cup.

clue.text: Not on strike? That's unusual!

parts.note: something not on is off
to beat something is to strike it

explanation.surface: A worker who is not taking industrial action is apparently a rarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on strike?' reads like a question about industrial action; the question mark warns that 'strike' means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat is a synonym for eccentric or unconventional, out of step with the norm.

clue.text: As such, do only upset religious class

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Strangely ordered words hint at a lesson about faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday school is a weekly class teaching children the faith, usually held at church.

clue.text: Scholar, male postal worker?

definitions.meaning: a learned writer or literary scholar
whimsically, a postman is a fellow who deals in mail, so a chap of the post

explanation.surface: Is a learned academic really just a postman?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is playful, signalled by the question mark: the letters are mail, not literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a literary scholar or writer, someone steeped in learning.

clue.text: A further section of orchestra not here

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: One more group of players is missing from the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean one more of the same kind, an additional one.

clue.text: Petite, the Spanish female elected

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a candidate elected is in

explanation.surface: A small Spanish woman has won an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate in build, like an elf, so a near synonym.

clue.text: Oscar training, sailor running

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
PE is physical education, training for the body
a rating is an ordinary sailor, not an officer

explanation.surface: Oscar is training while a sailor goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like part of the exercise scene but is the definition, as a machine is running.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is working or functioning, the same as running.

clue.text: Loose blouse — Georgia with blue one

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
blue jokes are ribald, crude or risqué
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman wears a loose top with something blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose high-necked blouse, named after the red shirts of the Italian patriot's followers.

clue.text: English artist showing age

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An English painter is getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, which age also means.

clue.text: Grasshopper in place close to desert

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of desert

explanation.surface: A grasshopper is found somewhere near the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a kind of large grasshopper that swarms, so an example of the wider group.

clue.text: Boat made from carbon, sign of things to come

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
an oracle is a prophecy, a message foretelling the future

explanation.surface: A vessel built from carbon fibre portends the future of boatbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: An oracle is usually the prophet, but the word also covers the prophecy delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wickerwork covered with hide, an example of a boat.

clue.text: Turncoat held by soldiers gets free

indicators.note: held by means the turncoat sits inside the soldiers, gripped by them

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side

explanation.surface: A deserter captured by troops is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' signals containment. 'free' looks like a verb about release but here means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without charge, so a synonym for free of cost.

clue.text: Grab small part

definitions.meaning: a short fragment, as of song or conversation

explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is both a quick grab and a brief fragment, as in a snatch of a tune.

clue.text: Prominent feature from the Left?

parts.note: from is the opposite of to, so the clue's words are flipped
left is the opposite of right, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A striking landmark seen from the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a trick: replace each word by its opposite, so 'from the Left' becomes 'to the right', giving TO and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or outcrop standing out on moorland, as on Dartmoor in England.

clue.text: Began struggling in lake in US resort

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the lake

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone started floundering in a lake while on holiday in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts the result inside the Scottish word for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Beach is a coastal city in southern California, an example of a US seaside resort.

clue.text: Strangely easy time, until now

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of easy come out oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Things have been oddly comfortable up to this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' is the anagram signal; 'time' giving T is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means up to the present moment, so a phrase meaning hitherto.

clue.text: Outdo former church leader in local

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of local

explanation.surface: A one-time vicar now holds court at the neighbourhood pub, the local.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's nearby pub; here it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass others, which is what outdoing them means.

clue.text: Boy happy heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: A cheerful boy sets off somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad is an informal synonym for a young male.

clue.text: Sporting cry from supporter wearing hot pants

indicators.note: wearing means the ally has the other letters around them like clothing
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of hot are messed up

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A fan in hot pants gives a hunting shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot pants' looks like clothing, but 'pants' is the anagram signal (British slang for rubbish) and 'wearing' puts the supporter inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the traditional hunting call on sighting a fox, so a cry from field sports.

clue.text: Prodigal son writer initially disowned, before the short break

parts.note: a pen is something you write with

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of disowned
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A wasteful son who writes is cut off from the family before a brief falling-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims THE to TH. 'Prodigal' looks like part of the parable but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means recklessly wasteful with money, and the answer is a person who squanders it.
